# Agent V2 LLM Maintenance Guide

This file is optimized for LLM agents maintaining this repository.

## Project Summary

Agent V2 is an installer and source package that generates portable agent
workflow configurations for Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.

The project goal is to keep one canonical set of role workflows and render it
into each supported harness using that harness's native files and conventions.
Installed projects should contain only runtime configuration. Source installer
files must stay in this repository.

## Core Concepts

- Harness: an AI coding environment. Supported harnesses are `codex`, `claude`,
  and `opencode`.
- Role: a named workflow agent, such as `xardas`, `gorn`, `lester`, or `lee`.
- Command: a slash workflow such as `/bookskeeper` or `/implement`.
- Provider: a model provider profile from `config/providers.json`.
- Tier: a provider-neutral model label: `fast`, `balanced`, `deep`, or `review`.
  The root/default agent has its separate `default` model mapping.
- Plugin: an optional integration from `config/plugins.json`, such as Graphify
  or context-mode.
- Installed setup: the generated runtime folder produced by `install.sh`.

## Source Of Truth

- `scripts/agent_setup.py`: installer and renderer for all generated runtime
  files, including harness profiles and the `coding-colony` launcher.
- `config/roles.json`: role metadata, tier, effort, sandbox, and summary.
- `core/shared-instructions.md`: behavioral rules rendered into every role.
- `core/role-workflows.md`: canonical role workflow bodies. Add or modify role
  behavior here first.
- `config/providers.json`: provider profiles and concrete model mappings.
- `config/plugins.json`: optional integration definitions and commands.
- `.env.example`: generated environment keys and comments.
- `tests/test_installation_integrity.py`: regression tests for generated output.
- `README.md`: user-facing project overview and installation guide.
- `AGENTS.md`: repository-level rules for agents working on this source package.

## Architecture Rules

Keep role behavior harness-neutral. Put shared behavior in
`core/shared-instructions.md` and role-specific behavior in
`core/role-workflows.md`; render both instead of duplicating either in generated
Codex, Claude, or OpenCode templates.

Keep harness-specific logic in `scripts/agent_setup.py`. Harness-specific logic
includes frontmatter, config format, MCP format, model resolution, plugin hooks,
and command binding.

Keep provider-specific model IDs out of role workflows and generated agent
frontmatter where tiers are supported. Use tier names in role definitions and
resolve concrete models through `.env` or harness config.

Keep optional integrations optional. Generated prompts may say a plugin is
enabled or disabled. Workflows that require a disabled or missing optional tool
must report the missing dependency instead of fabricating output.

Do not copy installer source files into installed projects. Runtime installs
should not contain source `install.sh`, `scripts/agent_setup.py`, `config/**`, or
`core/**`.

## Workflow Contracts

The public command set is `/spec`, `/refine`, `/analyze`, `/implement`,
`/verify`, and `/bookskeeper`. Every command must have a native binding in
Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.

- Milten returns `READY` or `NEEDS_INPUT` and keeps refined tasks focused on the
  business problem, observable behavior, scope, constraints, and acceptance
  criteria rather than implementation design.
- Lester returns `READY` or `BLOCKED`. A ready plan traces every requirement to
  repository evidence, file/symbol changes, tests, expected signals, and strict
  Lee review checks; it contains no unresolved material implementation choice.
- Gorn implements a ready plan and must delegate to Lee. A failing review starts
  another remediation, verification, and review cycle until Lee returns `PASS`
  or Gorn reports an external blocker. Changes with runtime-wiring risk require
  runnable startup/bootstrap evidence, not compilation alone.
- Scout is fast, low-effort, and read-only. Rhobar, Milten, Lester, and Xardas
  may use it for bounded repository discovery, but the parent validates all
  critical evidence and owns the output.
- Graphify is optional for general discovery and required for `/bookskeeper`.
  Repository-changing workflows mark `graphify-out/needs_update` when graph or
  guidance knowledge may be stale. Xardas runs `graphify update <repo>` for
  every existing graph, uses the marker to narrow documentation work, and
  clears it only after a successful refresh; it uses a deep build only when no
  graph exists.

## Adding A New Role

1. Add the role to `config/roles.json`.
2. Add the role name to `ROLE_ORDER` in `scripts/agent_setup.py`.
3. Add a matching `<!-- role: name -->` block in `core/role-workflows.md`.
4. If the role has a slash command, add it to `COMMAND_TO_ROLE` in
   `scripts/agent_setup.py`.
5. Update `README.md` if the role is user-facing.
6. Add or update tests in `tests/test_installation_integrity.py`.
7. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

## Adding A New Command

1. Add the command-to-role mapping to `COMMAND_TO_ROLE`.
2. Ensure the target role has a workflow in `core/role-workflows.md`.
3. Verify generated command files for Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode bind to
   the correct role.
4. Update README command documentation if user-facing.
5. Add test assertions for command binding.

## Adding A New Harness

1. Add the harness name to `SUPPORTED_HARNESSES`.
2. Add native provider behavior to `NATIVE_PROVIDER_BY_HARNESS`.
3. Implement a `generate_<harness>()` function in `scripts/agent_setup.py`.
4. Reuse `role_prompt()` so the harness receives canonical workflows.
5. Generate native command bindings where the harness supports them.
6. Add harness assertions to `tests/test_installation_integrity.py`.
7. Document install usage in `README.md`.

## Adding A New Provider

1. Add a profile to `config/providers.json`.
2. Declare `supported_harnesses`; list only harnesses that can resolve both the
   profile's model IDs and provider transport.
3. Provide all model tiers: `fast`, `balanced`, `deep`, and `review`. Keep the
   review model at least as capable as the deep model.
4. Add gateway fields when needed, such as base URL and API key env vars.
5. Update `.env.example` when new env vars are required.
6. Run the installer tests. They generate every supported provider/harness
   combination and reject incompatible combinations.

## Adding A New Optional Plugin

1. Add the plugin to `config/plugins.json`.
2. Add `install_command` and `install_description` when the dependency can be
   safely installed by a package manager.
3. Add `post_install_command` when the plugin also needs per-harness
   registration. Use `{platform}` as the selected harness placeholder.
4. Add generated runtime wiring in `scripts/agent_setup.py` only where needed.
5. Make prompts conditional on plugin enablement.
6. Log plugin status through `.env` fields such as `AGENT_PLUGINS`,
   `AGENT_OPTIONAL_DEPS`, and `AGENT_DETECTED_TOOLS`.
7. Log install and configuration attempts through `AGENT_PLUGIN_INSTALLS`.
8. Add integrity tests for generated config and optional behavior.

## OpenCode Model Tiers

OpenCode agent frontmatter should use tier names, for example `model: deep`.
The generated `model-tier-resolver.js` plugin resolves tiers from `.env` during
OpenCode config loading.

Do not put concrete provider IDs such as `openai/...` or `github-copilot/...`
inside generated OpenCode agent frontmatter.

Changing `.env` model values is picked up on OpenCode config reload or restart.
Do not promise live model hot-swapping inside an already-running session unless
OpenCode itself guarantees it.

OpenCode role agents must be `mode: subagent`; command files must set
`subtask: true`. Encode read-only and delegation boundaries in native
permissions instead of relying only on prose.

## Bookskeeper Contract

`/bookskeeper` must use the `xardas` workflow.

The Graphify plugin must be enabled and operational. If no graph exists, Xardas
creates a deep graph. For every existing graph, Xardas runs `graphify update
<repo>` before deriving guidance. `graphify-out/needs_update` narrows the
document refresh and is removed only after successful graph and document work.

Expected repository-owned outputs are:

- `graphify-out/CODE_CONVENTIONS.md`
- `graphify-out/TESTING.md`
- `graphify-out/BUSINESS_LOGIC.md`
- repo-local `AGENTS.md` managed section

Project-scoped docs under `AGENT_ROOT/docs/<project-slug>/` are allowed as
supporting material, but they are not a replacement for the repo-owned
Bookskeeper outputs.

## Testing

Run this after generator, provider, harness, role, command, or plugin changes:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Also run Python compile checks after editing installer code:

```bash
PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/private/tmp/agent-v2-oss-pycache python3 -m py_compile scripts/agent_setup.py tests/test_installation_integrity.py
```

For generated OpenCode JavaScript plugins, run `node --check` on the generated
plugin file in a temporary install or target install.

## Common Failure Modes

- Generated agents contain summaries but not real workflows: check
  `core/role-workflows.md` parsing and `role_prompt()` usage.
- Shared rules differ between roles: ensure `role_prompt()` renders
  `core/shared-instructions.md` rather than a hardcoded copy.
- Hardcoded provider models appear in agent files: check tier rendering and
  provider resolution.
- Optional tools are assumed when disabled: check plugin-conditional prompt
  text and generated `.env` fields.
- Missing optional tools are enabled but never installed: check
  `install_command`, `--install-missing-plugins`, interactive install prompts,
  and `AGENT_PLUGIN_INSTALLS`.
- Graphify is installed but not operational in a harness: check
  `post_install_command` and verify `graphify install --platform <harness>` was
  run for each selected harness.
- Installed folders contain source installer files: check copy/generation logic.
- OpenCode command delegates to the right agent but uses the wrong model: check
  generated tier frontmatter, `.env` model values, and `model-tier-resolver.js`.
- A harness is missing a command: verify all six bindings, including Claude
  `.claude/skills/<command>/SKILL.md` files.

## Maintenance Principles

- Prefer one canonical source and harness-specific renderers over duplicated
  workflow text.
- Keep README user-facing. Put maintainer details in this file.
- Keep tests focused on generated output integrity.
- Preserve user edits in installed `.env` when reinstalling without an explicit
  provider.
- Avoid broad rewrites. Generator changes should be small and covered by tests.
